identity.title: Inspiratory stridor at rest (audible without stethoscope)

technique.how: Listen without a stethoscope, close to the mouth and over the neck, for a harsh high-pitched sound; note whether it is inspiratory (extrathoracic/laryngeal obstruction), expiratory (intrathoracic), or biphasic (fixed, severe). Assess simultaneously for voice change, drooling, tongue/lip swelling, urticaria, tripod posture, and accessory muscle use.
technique.prerequisites: Quiet environment; do not delay treatment to complete the exam.
technique.contraindications: Do not lay the patient flat or instrument the pharynx in suspected supraglottic obstruction.

interpretation.positive_finding: Stridor at rest signals critical upper-airway narrowing; with urticaria, angioedema, or hypotension after an exposure it satisfies the airway criterion for anaphylaxis and mandates immediate intramuscular epinephrine and airway readiness.
interpretation.negative_finding: Absence of stridor does not exclude evolving airway compromise (angioedema, epiglottitis) or anaphylaxis with predominantly cutaneous, respiratory (wheeze), or circulatory features.
interpretation.pitfalls: Stridor can be mistaken for wheeze or transmitted upper-airway noise; it may disappear as obstruction becomes near-complete and airflow falls; vocal cord dysfunction mimics it.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive: treat as airway emergency (epinephrine if anaphylaxis, senior airway help, avoid sedation); negative: continue evaluation of other anaphylaxis criteria.

sources.citation: Cardona V, Ansotegui IJ, Ebisawa M, El-Gamal Y, Fernandez Rivas M, Fineman S, Geller M, Gonzalez-Estrada A, et al. World allergy organization anaphylaxis guidance 2020. World Allergy Organ J. 2020;13(10):100472.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Never wait for stridor to appear before treating suspected anaphylaxis or angioedema.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Stridor at rest with drooling, voice change, cyanosis, or falling saturation is an impending-airway-loss scenario - call anesthesia/ENT immediately and prepare for surgical airway.

extraction_notes: No JAMA RCE, meta-analysis, or prospective diagnostic-accuracy study of adult resting stridor was found: searches 'stridor sensitivity specificity upper airway obstruction adults', 'stridor[Title] adult emergency department', and 'stridor[Title] sensitivity specificity' returned predominantly pediatric/croup or unrelated records; none were fetched as accuracy sources. The WAO 2020 anaphylaxis guidance (confirmed PMID 33204386; PubMed record lists year 2025 for the 2020 article) supports stridor as a respiratory-compromise criterion by consensus. Record is therefore not_quantified.
